For many of the children of Israel, above all of the ten tribes, He delivered to their enemies, and nevertheless left them to harden in idolatry and their other sins, and so condemned them eternally. But in Ezechiel and Osee the Lord speaks of visitation taken in the first way. For of such reprobates, who are not visited by God with the fatherly rod, He Himself says in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:13|I let them go according to the desires of their heart|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]]. — Yet the words of God set down here can also be taken of the visitation of fatherly correction in the present, so that the sense is: Because I have known, loved and chosen you above the rest, therefore I will not spare you in the present, but will now punish all your vices, that you may cease from evil. For [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego enim quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. For to this end the Lord delivered them to their enemies, that those who were not corrected by the divine benefits might be amended by the torments of human cruelty. Hence in the second book of Machabees we have: [[2 Mach 6:13|For it is a token of great goodness, when sinners are not suffered to go on in their ways for a long time, but are presently punished|Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoris ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium]]. And again: [[2 Mach 6:14|not as with other nations|Non sicut in aliis nationibus]], [[2 Mach 6:14|whom the Lord patiently expecteth, that when the day of judgment shall come, he may punish them in the fulness of their sins|patienter Dominus exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies venerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat]]; [[2 Mach 6:15|Doth he also deal with us, so as to suffer our sins to come to their height, and then take vengeance on us|ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet]]. [[2 Mach 6:16|And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: but though he chastise his people with adversity he forsaketh them not|Propter quod nunquam quidem a nobis misericordiam suam amovet; corripiens vero, in adversis populum suum non derelinquit]].

paras.t: Consequenter inducit Amos sex exempla, ad ostendendum quod ultio populi a Deo illata, et per Prophetas annuntiata, sit justa: quatenus sicut exempla illa non fiunt, nisi certa causa exstiterit, ita non erit tribulatio, nisi per divinam justitiam rationabiliter inducatur seu dispensetur.
paras.en: Next Amos brings in six examples, to show that the punishment of the people, brought by God and announced through the Prophets, is just: so that, as the things in those examples do not happen unless there is a definite cause, so there will be no tribulation unless it is brought on or dispensed with good reason by the divine justice.

paras.t: Primum exemplum est: Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis, id est, nisi ex consensu vel rationabili causa, aut ex amicitia? quasi dicat, Non. Hoc communiter verum est; interdum tamen contingit, quod alius cogat alium ad proficiscendum secum. Sed Propheta loquitur secundum communem cursum. Per hanc autem convenientiam duorum simul euntium, mystice designatur concordia Dei et Prophetæ ex Dei ore loquentis.
paras.en: The first example is: [[3:3|Shall two walk together except they be agreed|Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis]], that is, unless by consent, or for some reasonable cause, or out of friendship? As if to say: No. This is commonly true; though sometimes it happens that one man compels another to travel with him. But the Prophet speaks according to the common course of things. Now by this agreement of two going together is mystically signified the concord of God and of the Prophet who speaks from the mouth of God.

paras.t: Secundum exemplum est: Numquid rugiet leo in saltu, id est inter arbores silvestres, nisi habuerit prædam, id est, nisi quum viderit aut adeptus fuerit animal quo vescatur? Quum enim patitur famem, mox ut viderit bestiam, dat rugitum: quo audito, territa bestia figit gradum, et capitur. Mystice, per rugitum leonis potest intelligi comminatio Christi (qui est leo de tribu Juda) per Prophetam: ad quam comminationem sequitur impiorum punitio, quemadmodum ad rugitum leonis prædæ voratio. Quidam tamen per leonem intelligunt dæmonem, qui tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret, semperque sitit animarum damnationem, et rugit ut eas deglutiat. — Tertium exemplum est, et redit in idem cum secundo: Numquid dabit catulus leonis vocem de cubili suo, id est de antro quo latitat, nisi aliquid apprehenderit, id est, nisi prædam cernat aut ceperit? quasi dicat, Non. Catulus iste potest intelligi vel Christus Filius Dei Patris, vel potestas adversa, sicut de leone jam dictum est.
paras.en: The second example is: [[3:4|Will a lion roar in the forest|Numquid rugiet leo in saltu]], that is, among the trees of the wood, [[3:4|if he have no prey|nisi habuerit prædam]], that is, unless he has seen or caught an animal to feed on? For when he suffers hunger, as soon as he sees a beast he gives a roar; and on hearing it the terrified beast stands rooted to the spot and is taken. Mystically, by the lion's roar can be understood the threatening of Christ (who is [[Apoc 5:5|the lion of the tribe of Juda|leo de tribu Juda]]) through the Prophet: upon which threatening follows the punishment of the wicked, as the devouring of the prey follows upon the lion's roar. Some, however, understand by the lion the devil, who [[1 Pet 5:8|as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret]], and ever thirsts for the damnation of souls, and roars to swallow them up. — The third example comes back to the same thing as the second: [[3:4|will the lion's whelp cry out of his den|Numquid dabit catulus leonis vocem de cubili suo]], that is, from the cave in which he lies hid, [[3:4|if he have taken nothing|nisi aliquid apprehenderit]], that is, unless he sees or has caught prey? As if to say: No. This whelp can be understood either as Christ, the Son of God the Father, or as the adverse power, as was just said of the lion.

paras.t: Quartum exemplum est: Numquid cadet avis in laqueum terræ, id est in rete super terram expansum, absque aucupe, id est sine artificio aucupis, qui fallit capitque volucres? Quidam aucupem accipiunt dæmonem, qui habentes alas virtutum et contemplationis interdum illaqueat, fallit, et ad peccati inducit ruinam. Alii autem per aucupem intelligunt Deum, qui impios comprehendit in laqueo pœnæ, juxta illud in Psalmo: Pluit super peccatores laqueos. Aliquando autem homines cadunt in laqueum culpæ propria inclinatione aut pravitate. Nam ut Origenes testatur, quamvis non essent diaboli, adhuc homines concupiscentiis pulsarentur. Dæmones tamen frequenter se miscent. — Quintum exemplum est: Numquid auferetur laqueus de terra, antequam quid ceperit? id est, rete ad capiendum aves expansum, non tollitur nisi aliquid comprehendat. Hoc communiter ita est. Per quod designatur, quod Deus non frustra aliquid inchoat, nec laqueos tormentorum impiis præparatos aufert, sed in eos projicit impœnitentes. Dæmon quoque non tollit laqueos tentationum, nisi ceperit aut vicerit aliquem.
paras.en: The fourth example is: [[3:5|Will the bird fall into the snare upon the earth|Numquid cadet avis in laqueum terræ]], that is, into a net spread out upon the ground, [[3:5|if there be no fowler|absque aucupe]], that is, without the craft of the fowler, who deceives and takes the birds? Some take the fowler to be the devil, who sometimes ensnares those that have the wings of the virtues and of contemplation, deceives them, and brings them down to the ruin of sin. Others understand by the fowler God, who catches the wicked in the snare of punishment, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 10:7|He shall rain snares upon sinners|Pluit super peccatores laqueos]]. Sometimes, however, men fall into the snare of guilt by their own inclination or depravity. For, as Origen testifies, even if there were no devils, men would still be assailed by concupiscences; yet the demons frequently mingle themselves in. — The fifth example is: [[3:5|Shall the snare be taken up from the earth, before it hath taken somewhat?|Numquid auferetur laqueus de terra, antequam quid ceperit?]] That is, a net spread out for catching birds is not taken up unless it catches something. This is commonly so. By which is signified that God does not begin anything in vain, nor does He take away the snares of torment prepared for the wicked, but casts the impenitent into them. The demon, too, does not take away the snares of temptation unless he has caught or overcome someone.

paras.t: Sextum exemplum est: Si clanget tuba in civitate, et populus non expavescet? id est, tuba non clanget in urbibus, adversariorum adventum insinuans, quin cives trepidabunt. Per quod designatur, quod in domo Ecclesiæ constituti, terreri debent audita voce sacræ Scripturæ, vel denuntiationis propheticæ, quæ significatur per tubam.
paras.en: The sixth example is: [[3:6|Shall the trumpet sound in a city, and the people not be afraid?|Si clanget tuba in civitate, et populus non expavescet?]] That is, the trumpet will not sound in cities, announcing the approach of enemies, without the citizens trembling. By which is signified that those set in the house of the Church ought to be struck with fear on hearing the voice of holy Scripture, or of the prophetic warning, which is signified by the trumpet.

paras.t: Hæc omnia introducta sunt ad significandum quam rationabile sit quod infertur: Si erit malum in civitate, id est, malum pœnæ seu justa punitio non erit in populo, quod Dominus non fecit, id est, non induxit, seu fieri ordinaverit aut permiserit in culpæ vindictam, aut aliam rationabilem causam, quatenus inordinatio culpæ ordinetur per inflictionem pœnæ? Quod fit, dum peccator qui propriam voluntatem contra Dei justitiam secutus est, cogitur per justitiam Dei sustinere quæ propria abhorret voluntas. De hoc malo pœnæ Dominus ait apud Isaiam: Ego Dominus, formans lucem, et creans tenebras, faciens pacem et creans malum; et Christus in Evangelio, Sufficit diei malitia sua. Est autem triplex malum, videlicet malum naturæ, ut monstruositas, malum culpæ, et malum pœnæ. Quibus aliqui addunt quartum malum, scilicet malum fortunæ, quod tamen ad malum pœnæ reducitur.
paras.en: All these things were brought in to show how reasonable is the conclusion drawn: [[3:6|Shall there be evil in a city|Si erit malum in civitate]], that is, there will be no evil of punishment, or just chastisement, among the people, [[3:6|which the Lord hath not done|quod Dominus non fecit]], that is, has not brought on, or ordained to be done, or permitted, in vengeance for guilt or for some other reasonable cause, so that the disorder of guilt may be set in order by the infliction of punishment. This happens when the sinner who has followed his own will against God's justice is compelled by God's justice to endure what his own will abhors. Of this evil of punishment the Lord says in Isaias: I the Lord, [[Is 45:7|I form the light, and create darkness, I make peace, and create evil|formans lucem, et creans tenebras, faciens pacem et creans malum]] [the passage has no margin reference]; and Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 6:34|Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof|Sufficit diei malitia sua]] [Latin *malitia*, here the same word-family as *malum*, "evil"]. Now evil is threefold, namely the evil of nature, such as monstrosity, the evil of guilt, and the evil of punishment. To these some add a fourth, namely the evil of fortune, which however is reduced to the evil of punishment.

paras.t: Quia non faciet Dominus verbum, id est factum notabile, necessarium vel utile sciri hominibus. Verbum autem frequenter pro re significata per verbum accipitur, quemadmodum Ezechias ait: Non fuit verbum in domo mea, quod non ostenderim eis. Quandoque vero accipitur pro interiori verbo seu conceptu mentali; aliquando autem pro verbo vocali. Nisi revelaverit secretum suum, id est factum tale, communi plebi incognitum, et naturaliter impræcognoscibile, qualia sunt futura contingentia, ad servos suos Prophetas: qui sunt amici Dei, ideo secreta sua revelat eis, tanquam familiaribus et amicis. Secundum Hieronymum, istud non est intelligendum de omnibus quæ Deus facit in cœlo, vel ante jam fecit, sed quæ in terra facturus est. Et puto quod maxime intelligatur de his quæ bonum communitatis concernunt. Sic enim mysteria Christi et Ecclesiæ, gestaque novi Testamenti prænuntiavit Patribus veteris Testamenti. Processum quoque et statum militantis Ecclesiæ prænuntiavit Apostolis, præsertim Joanni in Apocalypsi. Tempore quoque legis naturæ revelavit Noe futurum diluvium, Abrahæ et Lot subversionem Sodomæ. Jacob quoque in Genesi filiis suis ait: Congregamini, ut quæ ventura sunt in novissimis diebus, annuntiem vobis. Verum non singula singulis revelavit Prophetis, sed aliquibus plura, aliis pauciora. Divisiones enim gratiarum sunt, idem autem Spiritus, secundum Apostolum. Porro in his patet clementia et providentia Dei. Ideo enim futura supplicia primo Prophetis, deinde per eos prænuntiat populo, ut emendetur, et ab imminentibus eripiatur tormentis. In quo ostenditur Deus habere providentiam actuum humanorum, et omnia remunerare.
paras.en: [[3:7|For the Lord God doth nothing|Quia non faciet Dominus verbum]] [literally "the Lord will not do a *word*"], that is, a notable deed, one necessary or useful for men to know. For *word* is often taken for the thing signified by the word, as Ezechias says: [[Is 39:4|there was not any thing|Non fuit verbum]] in my house [[Is 39:4|which I have not shewn them|quod non ostenderim eis]] [no margin reference; the words are closest to Is 39:4, where the Vulgate has *res*, "thing", for Denis's *verbum*; the same story is at 4 Kings 20:15]. Sometimes, however, it is taken for the inner word or mental concept, and sometimes for the spoken word. [[3:7|without revealing his secret|Nisi revelaverit secretum suum]], that is, such a deed as is unknown to the common people and cannot naturally be foreknown, such as future contingents [that is, future events that depend on free choice or chance and so are not fixed by their causes], [[3:7|to his servants the prophets|ad servos suos Prophetas]]: who are God's friends, and so He reveals His secrets to them as to His intimates and friends. According to Jerome, this is not to be understood of all that God does in heaven, or has already done before, but of what He is going to do on earth. And I think it is understood above all of the things that concern the common good. For thus He foretold to the Fathers of the Old Testament the mysteries of Christ and of the Church and the deeds of the New Testament; He also foretold to the Apostles the course and state of the Church militant, especially to John in the Apocalypse. In the time of the law of nature, too, He revealed to Noe the coming flood[[Gen 6:7||]], and to Abraham and Lot the overthrow of Sodom[[Gen 18:20||]][[Gen 19:13||]]. Jacob, too, says to his sons in Genesis: [[Gen 49:1|Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days|Congregamini, ut quæ ventura sunt in novissimis diebus, annuntiem vobis]]. Yet He did not reveal everything to every Prophet, but more to some, less to others. For [[1 Cor 12:4|there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit|Divisiones enim gratiarum sunt, idem autem Spiritus]], according to the Apostle. In these things, moreover, the clemency and providence of God are plain. For He foretells future punishments first to the Prophets, then through them to the people, so that it may amend and be delivered from the torments that threaten it. In which it is shown that God has providence over human acts, and repays all things.

paras.t: Leo rugiet, quis non timebit? Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetabit? id est, si ad rugitum leonis homines et jumenta concutiuntur timore, multo amplius Deo jubente Vatibus ut prophetent, dignum est ut obediant. Itaque, Dominus Deus locutus est, id est, Prophetis annuntiavit occulta, et jussit ut ea patefaciant populo: quis eorum quibus Deus taliter est locutus, non prophetabit? id est, justum omnino est ut prophetent. Secundum Glossam, Amos iste quoniam pastor fuit, solitus timere leonem, timorem omnipotentis Dei, leonis rugitui comparat.
paras.en: [[3:8|The lion shall roar, who will not fear|Leo rugiet, quis non timebit]]? [[3:8|The Lord God hath spoken, who shall not prophesy?|Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetabit?]] That is, if at the lion's roar men and beasts are shaken with fear, much more, when God commands the seers to prophesy, is it fitting that they obey. And so: *The Lord God hath spoken*, that is, He has announced hidden things to the Prophets and commanded them to make them known to the people: *who* of those to whom God has so spoken *shall not prophesy*? That is, it is altogether right that they prophesy. According to the Gloss, this Amos, since he was a shepherd[[Amos 1:1||]] accustomed to fear the lion, compares the fear of almighty God to the roar of a lion.

paras.t: Consequenter Deus volens universis judiciorum suorum contra Israel æquitatem ostendere, ait: Auditum facite, id est, manifestate, o Prophetæ, vel alii a Prophetis edocti, in ædibus Azoti, id est in domibus urbis Philistinorum sic dictæ, et in ædibus terræ Ægypti; et dicite: Congregamini, id est, convenite, o Azotii atque Ægyptii, super montes Samariæ. Potest per Samariam intelligi ipsa metropolis decem tribuum, vel tota provincia montibus plena. Et videte a locis sublimibus insanias multas, id est vitia idololatriæ, aliaque irrationabilissima scelera, quæ naturalis ratio detestatur, in medio ejus, puta Samariæ; videte quoque et calumniam patientes, id est pauperes et simplices quibus injuriantur potentes ac divites, in penetralibus ejus, id est secretioribus habitaculis Samariæ.
paras.en: Next God, wishing to show to all the equity of His judgments against Israel, says: [[3:9|Publish it|Auditum facite]], that is, make it known, O Prophets, or others taught by the Prophets, [[3:9|in the houses of Azotus|in ædibus Azoti]], that is, in the houses of the city of the Philistines so called, [[3:9|and in the houses of the land of Egypt|et in ædibus terræ Ægypti]]; [[3:9|and say|et dicite]]: [[3:9|Assemble yourselves|Congregamini]], that is, come together, O men of Azotus and of Egypt, [[3:9|upon the mountains of Samaria|super montes Samariæ]]. By Samaria can be understood the capital itself of the ten tribes, or the whole province, which is full of mountains. [[3:9|and behold|Et videte]] from the high places [[3:9|the many follies|insanias multas]], that is, the vices of idolatry and other most irrational crimes, which natural reason abhors, [[3:9|in the midst thereof|in medio ejus]], namely of Samaria; behold also [[3:9|them that suffer oppression|et calumniam patientes]], that is, the poor and simple, whom the powerful and rich wrong, [[3:9|in the inner rooms thereof|in penetralibus ejus]], that is, in the more hidden dwellings of Samaria.

paras.t: Et nescierunt decem tribus facere rectum, dicit Dominus, id est opera bona et justa, quoniam excæcavit eos sua malitia. Sed ista ignorantia juris, seu desiderata, non excusat. De talibus loquitur Jeremias: Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Thesaurizantes iniquitatem, id est peccata peccatis adjicientes, et incessabiliter accumulantes, et rapinam, id est bona aliis violenter ablata, in ædibus, id est domibus suis, in quibus ista spoliata reponunt.
paras.en: [[3:10|And they have not known|Et nescierunt]], the ten tribes, [[3:10|to do the right thing, saith the Lord|facere rectum, dicit Dominus]], that is, good and just works, since their malice blinded them. But this ignorance of the law, being as it were desired [that is, wilful ignorance, which does not excuse but rather aggravates the sin], does not excuse. Of such men Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[3:10|storing up iniquity|Thesaurizantes iniquitatem]], that is, adding sins to sins and heaping them up without ceasing, [[3:10|and robberies|et rapinam]], that is, goods taken from others by violence, [[3:10|in their houses|in ædibus]], that is, in their dwellings, in which they store up these spoils.

paras.t: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Tribulabitur et circuietur terra, id est, plebs decem tribuum ab Assyriis affligetur et circumdata erit. Quod factum est tempore Salmanasar regis Assyriorum. Et detrahetur ex te fortitudo tua, id est regia dignitas seu potestas; vel, potentes tui, o decem tribus, superabuntur; et diripientur ædes tuæ, id est, habitacula tua spoliabuntur ac destruentur.
paras.en: [[3:11|Therefore thus saith the Lord God|Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus]]: [[3:11|The land shall be in tribulation, and shall be compassed about|Tribulabitur et circuietur terra]], that is, the people of the ten tribes will be afflicted and surrounded by the Assyrians. This was done in the time of Salmanasar king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:3||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]]. [[3:11|and thy strength shall be taken away from thee|Et detrahetur ex te fortitudo tua]], that is, the royal dignity or power; or, thy mighty men, O ten tribes, will be overcome; [[3:11|and thy houses shall be spoiled|et diripientur ædes tuæ]], that is, thy dwellings will be plundered and destroyed.

paras.t: Quoniam tamen non omnes de decem tribubus perituri erant, subjungitur (utitur quoque Amos parabola sumpta ex suo officio): Hæc dicit Dominus: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura aut extremum auriculæ, id est parvas paucasque reliquias; sic eruentur filii Israel qui habitant in Samaria, id est provincia illa, ita quod pauci eorum evadent sævitiam Assyriorum, in plaga lectuli et in Damasci grabato: id est, isti qui corporaliter habitabant in Samaria, habitabant, id est animo quiescebant, in plaga, id est regione, lectuli, id est regis ac populi Syriæ: quia Phacee rex Israel et populus ejus vel etiam posteri, in Rasin rege Syriæ et populo ejus confidebant, quos conduxerunt ad pugnandum contra Juda tempore Achaz; sicque in eis et in grabato Damasci, id est populo urbis illius, quasi in lecto quiescebant, magnam in illis habendo fiduciam. Sic exponit Hieronymus. Alii autem exponunt sic: In plaga lectuli, id est, prædicti ab Assyriis eruentur, et morabuntur seu erunt, postquam evaserunt, in regione Juda, quæ dicitur lectulus propter templum situm in ea, quod erat quasi lectus Sponsi cœlestis. Unde secundo Paralipomenon scriptum est, quod quidam eorum ad exhortationem Ezechiæ venerunt Jerusalem et ad cultum Dei conversi sunt. Aliqui vero ad Damascum fugerunt, ut dicunt: ideoque subjungitur, In Damasci grabato.
paras.en: Since, however, not all of the ten tribes were to perish, there is added (and Amos uses a parable taken from his own calling): [[3:12|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[3:12|As if a shepherd should get out of the lion's mouth two legs, or the tip of the ear|Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura aut extremum auriculæ]], that is, small and scanty remnants; [[3:12|so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria|sic eruentur filii Israel qui habitant in Samaria]], that is, in that province, so that few of them will escape the savagery of the Assyrians, [[3:12|in a place of a bed, and in the couch of Damascus|in plaga lectuli et in Damasci grabato]]: that is, those who dwelt bodily in Samaria dwelt, that is, rested in mind, *in the place*, that is, the region, *of a bed*, that is, of the king and people of Syria: for Phacee king of Israel and his people, or also their descendants, trusted in Rasin king of Syria and his people, whom they hired to fight against Juda in the time of Achaz[[4 Kings 16:5||]]; and so they rested in them, and *in the couch of Damascus*, that is, in the people of that city, as in a bed, putting great trust in them. So Jerome expounds it. But others expound it thus: *In a place of a bed*, that is, the aforesaid will be taken out from the Assyrians, and will stay or be, after they have escaped, in the region of Juda, which is called a bed because of the temple situated in it, which was as it were the bed of the heavenly Bridegroom. Hence it is written in the second book of Paralipomenon that some of them, at the exhortation of Ezechias, came to Jerusalem and were converted to the worship of God[[2 Par 30:11||]]. Others, as they say, fled to Damascus; and therefore it is added, *In the couch of Damascus*.

paras.t: Audite, o Prophetæ, revelationes prophetales auribus cordis, et contestamini, id est, cum attestatione seu firmiter prædicate eas, in domo Jacob, id est familia decem tribuum descendentium de semine Jacob, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum.
paras.en: [[3:13|Hear ye|Audite]], O Prophets, the prophetic revelations with the ears of the heart, [[3:13|and testify|et contestamini]], that is, preach them with solemn witness, or firmly, [[3:13|in the house of Jacob|in domo Jacob]], that is, in the family of the ten tribes descended from the seed of Jacob, [[3:13|saith the Lord the God of hosts|dicit Dominus Deus exercituum]].

paras.t: Quia in die quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel super eum, id est, quum per regem Assyriorum Salmanasar cœpero peccata decem tribuum vindicare in eas, visitabo super altaria Bethel, id est, sacrilega altaria facta in urbe nomine Bethel, destruam per Assyrios; et amputabuntur cornua altaris principalis aurei vituli, qui positus fuit in Bethel, et cadent in terram: Assyrii namque omnia loca et fana idololatriæ decem tribuum destruxerunt.
paras.en: [[3:14|That in the day when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel|Quia in die quum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israel]] [[3:14|upon him|super eum]], that is, when through Salmanasar king of the Assyrians I shall begin to punish the sins of the ten tribes upon them, [[3:14|I will visit|visitabo]] [[3:14|upon the altars of Bethel|super altaria Bethel]], that is, I will destroy through the Assyrians the sacrilegious altars made in the city named Bethel[[3 Kings 12:32||]] [the margin reads III Reg. xxii, 32; the altar at Bethel is at 3 Kings 12:32]; [[3:14|and the horns of the altars shall be cut off|et amputabuntur cornua altaris]], the chief altar, of the golden calf that was set up in Bethel, [[3:14|and shall fall to the ground|et cadent in terram]]: for the Assyrians destroyed all the places and shrines of idolatry of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Et percutiam domum hiemalem cum domo æstiva, id est, omnes domos earum, tam illas in quibus manebant tempore hiemali seu frigido, quam illas in quibus æstivo tempore morabantur, per exercitum Assyriorum demoliar. Quamvis enim Assyrii ista fecerunt mala intentione et cum gravi peccato, Deus tamen juste induxit eos ad hæc, tanquam ad rem bonam seu justam punitionem. Potentes autem et divites decem tribuum, duas domos habebant: unam hiemalem, respicientem ad austrum, unde calidus ventus exsurgit; aliam æstivalem, versam ad aquilonem, unde frigidus nascitur ventus: ut secundum varietatem temporum, apta ac delectabilia habitacula inhabitarent. Et peribunt domus eburneæ: qualem legitur Achab ædificasse. Dicuntur autem eburneæ, quoniam quædam structuræ de ebore factæ, erant in eis. Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ, dicit Dominus. Assyrii enim plurimas domos subverterunt.
paras.en: [[3:15|And I will strike the winter house with the summer house|Et percutiam domum hiemalem cum domo æstiva]], that is, I will pull down by the army of the Assyrians all their houses, both those in which they lived in the winter or cold season and those in which they stayed in the summer season. For although the Assyrians did these things with an evil intention and with grievous sin, God nevertheless justly led them to it, as to a good thing, that is, a just punishment. Now the powerful and rich of the ten tribes had two houses: one for winter, facing the south, whence the warm wind rises; the other for summer, turned towards the north, whence the cold wind springs: so that, according to the change of seasons, they might live in fitting and pleasant dwellings. [[3:15|and the houses of ivory shall perish|Et peribunt domus eburneæ]]: such a one as Achab is read to have built[[3 Kings 22:39||]]. And they are called houses of ivory because certain parts of their structure were made of ivory. [[3:15|and many houses shall be destroyed, saith the Lord|Et dissipabuntur ædes multæ, dicit Dominus]]. For the Assyrians overthrew very many houses.
